You are a corporate wellness coordinator responsible for launching an employee lunch program. Your goal is to create a dietary preference survey, select recipes that match common employee preferences, plan a weekly menu, build a recipe knowledge base, and communicate the program to staff.

Start by reading the Cafeteria_Budget.pdf in your workspace, which describes the budget per meal and expected headcount. Also review the dietary_requirements.json file that lists common dietary restrictions and allergen considerations for the employee population.

Create a dietary preference survey using the forms platform. The survey should be titled "Employee Lunch Program Preferences" and include the following five questions: a multiple choice question asking about preferred cuisine type with options Chinese Meat Dishes, Chinese Vegetable Dishes, Chinese Staple Foods, Soups, and Seafood; a multiple choice question about spice tolerance with options Mild, Medium, and Spicy; a multiple choice question about dietary restrictions with options Vegetarian, No Pork, No Seafood, Gluten Free, and No Restrictions; a short text question asking how important variety is in their lunch options (rate on a scale of 1 to 5); and a short text question for any additional food preferences or allergies.

Query the recipe database to find recipes across different categories. Search for at least two meat dishes, two vegetable dishes, one staple food, one soup, and one seafood dish. For each recipe retrieved, note the recipe name, category, difficulty level, and ingredients list.

Write a Python script called menu_planner.py in your workspace and execute it using command-line tools. The script should select five recipes for a Monday through Friday weekly menu, choosing recipes that balance different categories (no two consecutive days with the same category) and keeping difficulty at 4 or below for cafeteria feasibility. The script should estimate a cost per serving of 8 dollars for meat and seafood dishes, 5 dollars for vegetable dishes, 6 dollars for staple foods, and 4 dollars for soups, then compute the total weekly cost assuming 50 servings per day.

Create an Excel workbook called Meal_Program_Plan.xlsx in your workspace with four sheets.

The first sheet should be named Survey_Questions and contain columns for question_num, text, and type. Include one row for each of the five survey questions.

The second sheet should be named Recipe_Selection and contain columns for recipe_name, category, and difficulty. Include one row for each recipe you retrieved from the recipe database, with at least seven recipes total. Record the recipe name and category exactly as returned by the recipe database.

The third sheet should be named Weekly_Menu and contain columns for day, lunch_recipe, and estimated_cost. Include five rows, one for each weekday Monday through Friday, with the assigned recipe and estimated cost per serving. Enter all cost figures as literal numbers (for example, 8), not as spreadsheet formulas.

The fourth sheet should be named Program_Summary and contain columns for metric and value. Include rows for total_weekly_cost (sum of daily cost times 50 servings), avg_daily_cost_per_person, survey_question_count (5), recipes_evaluated (total recipes retrieved), and menu_days (5).

Set up a database in the team wiki system called "Recipe Knowledge Base" with properties for Recipe Name (title), Category (select with options for the main recipe categories), Difficulty (number), and Suitable For (multi-select with options Lunch, Dinner, Quick Meal). Add one entry for each recipe you included in the weekly menu.

Send an email to all_staff@company.com with the subject "New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey" describing the new lunch program, mentioning that the weekly menu has been planned with a variety of dishes, and encouraging employees to fill out the dietary preference survey to help improve future menu selections.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, keep recipe search on explore, keep the form write on the workflow operator, keep `menu_planner.py` on one local writer, then parallelize the workbook, Notion, and email. A wave must finish and return all stated handoffs before the next wave begins.

Before Wave 1, the main agent reads `Cafeteria_Budget.pdf` and `dietary_requirements.json` in read-only mode and freezes the per-meal budget, headcount, and dietary restrictions.

1. Wave 1 — dispatch exactly 2 sub-agents in parallel:

   1. explore 0 (web-domain-researcher 0): Recipe owner. Retrieve at least 7 recipes from the recipe database — at least 2 Chinese Meat Dishes, 2 Chinese Vegetable Dishes, 1 Chinese Staple Foods, 1 Soups, and 1 Seafood — recording each recipe's name, category, difficulty, and ingredients exactly as returned. Return the compact recipe rows plus category/count controls. Do not write files, create the form, or run the planner.
   2. coder 0 (external-workflow-operator 0): Sole owner of the Google Form `Employee Lunch Program Preferences`. Search the exact title first, create it once only when absent, and block on duplicates. Add, in order, three multiple-choice questions — preferred cuisine type (Chinese Meat Dishes / Chinese Vegetable Dishes / Chinese Staple Foods / Soups / Seafood), spice tolerance (Mild / Medium / Spicy), and dietary restrictions (Vegetarian / No Pork / No Seafood / Gluten Free / No Restrictions) — and two short-text questions on the importance of variety (rate 1 to 5) and any other food preferences or allergies. Retrieve the form to verify the title, question wording, options, and question types. Do not query recipes or write the planner.

After Wave 1, the main agent freezes the retrieved recipe list and the form ID/title/URL. Missing recipes or an ambiguous form create is a blocker.

2. Wave 2 — dispatch exactly 1 coder sub-agent:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 0): Sole owner of `menu_planner.py`. It receives the frozen recipes, budget, and dietary restrictions. Write and run the script embedding this data and selecting exactly 5 recipes for Monday through Friday, with difficulty <= 4, no category repeating on consecutive days, and dietary restrictions honored where possible (avoid pork if No Pork, avoid seafood if No Seafood); apply frozen per-serving costs of 8 USD for meat and seafood dishes, 5 USD for vegetable dishes, 6 USD for staple foods, and 4 USD for soups. Return the selected weekly menu, per-day costs, and total weekly cost (sum of the 5 per-serving costs times 50 servings per day). Do not create the workbook, Notion database, form, or email.

After Wave 2, the main agent verifies and freezes the weekly menu and cost totals as the sole downstream source.

3. Wave 3 — dispatch exactly 3 coder sub-agents in parallel:

   1. coder 0 (office-report-builder 1): Sole writer of `Meal_Program_Plan.xlsx`. Read only the frozen recipes, menu, and survey question list. Create exactly four worksheets: `Survey_Questions` holds `question_num/text/type` with exactly the 5 survey questions; `Recipe_Selection` holds `recipe_name/category/difficulty` with at least 7 rows (2 meat, 2 vegetable, 1 staple, 1 soup, 1 seafood, names and categories exactly as retrieved); `Weekly_Menu` holds `day/lunch_recipe/estimated_cost` with exactly 5 rows for Monday-Friday, costs entered as literal numbers per the pricing (meat/seafood 8, vegetable 5, staple 6, soup 4 USD); `Program_Summary` holds metric/value rows — `total_weekly_cost` (sum of daily estimated_cost x 50 servings), `avg_daily_cost_per_person` (total / (5 days x 50 servings)), `survey_question_count` = 5, `recipes_evaluated` (count of Recipe_Selection rows), and `menu_days` = 5 — all as literal numbers rather than formulas. Read every populated range back.
   2. coder 1 (external-workflow-operator 1): Sole Notion owner of the database `Recipe Knowledge Base`. Search the exact title first, create it once only when absent, and reuse without duplicating. Require properties Recipe Name (title), Category (select: Chinese Meat Dishes, Chinese Vegetable Dishes, Chinese Staple Foods, Soups, Seafood), Difficulty (number), and Suitable For (multi-select: Lunch, Dinner, Quick Meal). Add exactly 5 entries — one per recipe from the frozen Monday-Friday weekly menu — with recipe name, category, and difficulty (<= 4) copied exactly and Suitable For including at least `Lunch`. Read back and require exactly 5 pages.
   3. coder 2 (external-workflow-operator 2): Sole email owner. Search Sent mail for exact To `all_staff@company.com` / subject `New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey`, send at most once, then read it back. The body introduces the lunch program, mentions the planned weekly menu with dishes across meat, vegetable, staple, soup, and seafood categories, and encourages employees to complete `Employee Lunch Program Preferences`, including the survey link if available, otherwise referencing the survey by its exact title.

After Wave 3, the main agent reconciles the workbook, Notion five-page set, form, and email against the same frozen menu. Do not dispatch more sub-agents.

You are a recipe researcher for a corporate cafeteria lunch program. Your ONLY job is to retrieve recipes from the recipe database (the howtocook MCP server) and report them back. Do NOT create any files, forms, spreadsheets, Notion databases, or emails. Do NOT run any planner scripts.

Use the howtocook MCP tools:
- mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipesByCategory (categories: 水产, 早餐, 调料, 甜品, 饮品, 荤菜, 半成品加工, 汤, 主食, 素菜)
- mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getAllRecipes
- mcp__howtocook__mcp_howtocook_getRecipeById (to fetch full details for specific recipes)

Required retrieval targets (must retrieve at least 7 recipes total):
- At least 2 Chinese Meat Dishes (category 荤菜)
- At least 2 Chinese Vegetable Dishes (category 素菜)
- At least 1 Chinese Staple Food (category 主食)
- At least 1 Soup (category 汤)
- At least 1 Seafood dish (category 水产)

For EACH recipe you retrieve, record EXACTLY as returned by the database:
1. recipe name (verbatim, in the original language as returned)
2. category (verbatim, e.g. 荤菜/素菜/主食/汤/水产)
3. difficulty level (the numeric difficulty rating from the database)
4. ingredients list (as returned)

First call getAllRecipes or getRecipesByCategory to see what's available, then call getRecipeById for each recipe you need details on. Pick recipes with difficulty <= 4 where possible (prefer them, but report the difficulty exactly as returned regardless). Aim to fetch at least 7-10 recipes to give the planner a good pool (e.g. 3 meat, 2-3 vegetable, 2 staple, 2 soup, 2 seafood if available).

Return a compact, structured report:
- A table/list of recipe rows: name | category | difficulty | ingredients (ingredients can be summarized but keep the full list)
- Category/count control: how many recipes were found per category (荤菜, 素菜, 主食, 汤, 水产)
- Explicitly state if any required category had fewer than the target number of recipes.

Your final output must contain every recipe name exactly as it appears in the database, since downstream consumers will copy names verbatim.
Retrieve recipes from database

You are the sole owner of `menu_planner.py` for a corporate cafeteria lunch program. Your ONLY job: write the script in the workspace, run it, and report the results. Do NOT create any Excel workbook, Notion database, Google Form, or email. Do NOT modify anything else.

WORKSPACE: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-howtocook-gform-excel-notion-email/workspace
Write the file as menu_planner.py in that directory. Run it with the python command via the terminal tool (or python_execute with the file path).

FROZEN RECIPE POOL (name, category, difficulty) — categories are the Chinese labels exactly as returned by the recipe database; treat 荤菜=Meat, 素菜=Vegetable, 主食=Staple, 汤=Soup, 水产=Seafood:
1. 可乐鸡翅的做法, 荤菜, 3
2. 小炒肉的做法, 荤菜, 3   (NOTE: contains pork 五花肉)
3. 孜然牛肉的做法, 荤菜, 3
4. 地三鲜的做法, 素菜, 3
5. 酸辣土豆丝的做法, 素菜, 2
6. 蚝油生菜的做法, 素菜, 2
7. 蛋炒饭的做法, 主食, 3
8. 葱油拌面的做法, 主食, 2
9. 西红柿鸡蛋汤的做法, 汤, 2
10. 紫菜蛋花汤的做法, 汤, 2   (NOTE: contains optional shrimp 虾仁)
11. 白灼虾的做法, 水产, 2
12. 清蒸鲈鱼的做法, 水产, 3

FROZEN PROGRAM FACTS:
- Per-serving cost by category (USD): meat (荤菜) = 8, seafood (水产) = 8, vegetable (素菜) = 5, staple (主食) = 6, soup (汤) = 4
- Servings per day: 50; program days: Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday, Friday
- Selection rules: difficulty must be <= 4; NO two consecutive days with the same category; dietary restrictions in the employee population include "No Pork" and "No Seafood" — honor where possible (prefer chicken/beef meat dishes over the pork-containing 小炒肉; avoid the optional-shrimp soup 紫菜蛋花汤).
- Goal: maximize category variety — aim for a 5-day menu that uses FIVE DIFFERENT categories (one per day: meat, vegetable, staple, soup, seafood) so no consecutive-day repeat is trivially satisfied and the menu showcases variety.

SCRIPT REQUIREMENTS (menu_planner.py):
- Embed the 12-recipe pool (name, category, difficulty) and the cost table directly in the script as data structures.
- Implement a deterministic selection algorithm: filter difficulty <= 4; drop 小炒肉 (pork, conflicts with No Pork) and 紫菜蛋花汤 (shrimp, conflicts with No Seafood) from consideration; then pick exactly 5 recipes for Mon-Fri covering 5 distinct categories (one per day). Order the days so no two consecutive days share a category (all distinct, so any order works; use a sensible order, e.g. Mon meat, Tue vegetable, Wed staple, Thu soup, Fri seafood).
- Compute per-day estimated cost per serving from the category cost table, and total weekly cost = sum of the 5 per-serving costs × 50 servings/day.
- Print a clear report: each day (Monday–Friday) with recipe name, category, difficulty, estimated cost per serving; then total weekly cost; then avg daily cost per person = total weekly cost / (5 days × 50 servings).
- The script must run successfully with python and print the report. Make sure the recipe names and categories are printed EXACTLY as in the pool above (verbatim Chinese characters, including "的做法" suffix).

RETURN (structured report):
- The exact 5-day weekly menu: day | recipe_name (verbatim) | category (Chinese, verbatim) | difficulty | estimated_cost (per serving)
- total_weekly_cost (USD, = sum of 5 per-serving costs × 50)
- avg_daily_cost_per_person (USD)
- Confirmation that the script file exists at /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731/SingleUserTurn-terminal-howtocook-gform-excel-notion-email/workspace/menu_planner.py and the exact stdout of the run (or at least the numbers).
- State any deviation from the rules if forced by the data.
Write and run menu_planner.py

Your ONLY job: create this workbook with exactly the four worksheets and content described below, then read every populated range back to verify. Do NOT create or modify the Google Form, Notion database, email, or menu_planner.py.

If the file does not exist, create it with mcp__excel__create_workbook (which creates a default sheet — rename or reuse it as the first sheet, or delete the default after creating your four sheets). Use mcp__excel__create_worksheet for the other sheets, mcp__excel__write_data_to_excel to write data, mcp__excel__rename_worksheet / mcp__excel__delete_worksheet as needed. 葱油拌面的做法 | 主食 | 2
西红柿鸡蛋汤的做法 | 汤 | 2
紫菜蛋花汤的做法 | 汤 | 2
白灼虾的做法 | 水产 | 2
清蒸鲈鱼的做法 | 水产 | 3
(12 rows total — at least 7 required: 3 meat 荤菜, 3 vegetable 素菜, 2 staple 主食, 2 soup 汤, 2 seafood 水产)

WEEKLY MENU (5 rows) — sheet Weekly_Menu, columns: day | lunch_recipe | estimated_cost
Monday | 可乐鸡翅的做法 | 8

PROGRAM SUMMARY — sheet Program_Summary, columns: metric | value, with these rows (all values literal numbers, NOT formulas):
total_weekly_cost | 1550
avg_daily_cost_per_person | 6.2

recipes_evaluated | 12
menu_days | 5
(Note: total_weekly_cost = (8+5+6+4+8) × 50 servings = 1550; avg_daily_cost_per_person = 1550 / (5 days × 50 servings) = 6.2)

VERIFICATION REQUIREMENTS:
- After writing, call mcp__excel__get_workbook_metadata to confirm exactly four worksheets with the exact names: Survey_Questions, Recipe_Selection, Weekly_Menu, Program_Summary.
- Read back EVERY populated range (headers + all rows) on each sheet with mcp__excel__read_data_from_excel and confirm values match the frozen data above (recipe names and categories character-for-character).

RETURN a structured report:

You are the sole Notion owner of a database titled "Recipe Knowledge Base" for a corporate lunch program. Your ONLY job: create (or reuse) this database with the exact schema below, add exactly 5 entries from the frozen weekly menu, and verify. Do NOT create the Excel workbook, Google Form, or email.

STEPS:
1. Search Notion for an existing database with the exact title "Recipe Knowledge Base" (use mcp__notion__API-post-search with query "Recipe Knowledge Base"). If an existing database with that exact title already exists, reuse it WITHOUT duplicating. If it does not exist, create it once using mcp__notion__API-create-a-database (parent can be a page found via search, e.g. search with empty query to find an available page; if a suitable parent page exists use its id).

   - "Recipe Name" (type: title)
   - "Category" (type: select) with options exactly: "Chinese Meat Dishes", "Chinese Vegetable Dishes", "Chinese Staple Foods", "Soups", "Seafood"
   - "Difficulty" (type: number)
   - "Suitable For" (type: multi_select) with options exactly: "Lunch", "Dinner", "Quick Meal"
   (If reusing an existing database, update properties as needed with mcp__notion__API-update-a-database; if creating fresh, pass the property schema in the create call.)
3. Add EXACTLY 5 pages (one per weekday recipe from the frozen menu) via mcp__notion__API-post-page with parent.database_id = the database id. Category values use the English select option names; Difficulty is the numeric difficulty; Suitable For must include "Lunch" (you may also add "Dinner" and/or "Quick Meal" if sensible, but "Lunch" is required):

   a. Recipe Name: 可乐鸡翅的做法 | Category: Chinese Meat Dishes | Difficulty: 3 | Suitable For: Lunch, Dinner
   b. Recipe Name: 地三鲜的做法 | Category: Chinese Vegetable Dishes | Difficulty: 3 | Suitable For: Lunch
   c. Recipe Name: 蛋炒饭的做法 | Category: Chinese Staple Foods | Difficulty: 3 | Suitable For: Lunch, Quick Meal
   d. Recipe Name: 西红柿鸡蛋汤的做法 | Category: Soups | Difficulty: 2 | Suitable For: Lunch
   e. Recipe Name: 白灼虾的做法 | Category: Seafood | Difficulty: 2 | Suitable For: Lunch, Dinner

   Recipe names MUST be copied exactly (including "的做法" suffix).
4. Verify by querying the database with mcp__notion__API-post-database-query (database_id) and read back all pages. REQUIRE exactly 5 pages, with Recipe Name, Category, Difficulty, and Suitable For matching the frozen data above.

RETURN a structured report:
- database_id
- database title (exact)
- Confirmed property schema (Recipe Name/title, Category/select + its options, Difficulty/number, Suitable For/multi_select + its options)
- The 5 page entries read back (name, category, difficulty, suitable_for) and confirmation that exactly 5 pages exist
- Confirmation that no duplicate database was created
Create Notion Recipe Knowledge Base

You are the sole email owner for a corporate lunch program announcement. Your ONLY job: send ONE email to all_staff@company.com with the exact subject "New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey", then read it back to verify. Do NOT create the Excel workbook, Notion database, or Google Form (the form already exists).

STEPS:
1. FIRST search the email server for any previously sent email to all_staff@company.com with subject "New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey" (use mcp__emails__search_emails with query like "New Employee Lunch Program" and check Sent folder if available). If an identical email already exists in Sent, do NOT send a duplicate — report it and read it back instead. Otherwise send exactly one email.
2. Send with mcp__emails__send_email:
   - to: all_staff@company.com
   - subject: New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey
   - body: a friendly announcement that includes ALL of the following:
     * Introduction of the new Employee Lunch Program (corporate cafeteria lunch program)
     * Mention that a weekly menu (Monday–Friday) has been planned with a variety of dishes across categories: meat dishes, vegetable dishes, staple foods, soups, and seafood
     * Mention the menu was planned with dietary considerations (pork-free and seafood-conscious options, vegetarian options) and difficulty levels suitable for cafeteria preparation
     * Encourage employees to fill out the dietary preference survey titled "Employee Lunch Program Preferences" to help improve future menu selections
     * Include the survey link: https://docs.google.com/forms/d/aa23da94-09c3-4d01-b7df-ea40877695fe/viewform
   - A plain-text body is fine; you may optionally include a matching html_body.
3. After sending, read it back: search Sent (mcp__emails__search_emails in the Sent folder, or get emails from Sent folder) for the message, and confirm: To = all_staff@company.com, Subject = "New Employee Lunch Program - Take Our Survey", and the body contains the required elements. Report the email id.

RETURN a structured report:
- email id
- To / Subject (exact) / From (if shown)
- Confirmation of exactly one email sent (no duplicate)
- Brief confirmation that the body mentions the planned weekly menu with variety across meat/vegetable/staple/soup/seafood, dietary considerations, and the survey encouragement with the survey link/title
- If a pre-existing identical email was found instead, state that and show its id.
Send employee lunch program email
